name: City bu city (city不city)
blurb: Chinese slang for "Is it trendy or not?", from an American creator's 2024 videos
title: City Bu City (city不city) Meaning: China's 2024 Viral Meme
description: "City不city" is Chinese slang meaning "Is it trendy and modern or not?". It comes from American creator 保保熊's China travel videos, a Douyin hit in June 2024.
answer: "City不city" (city bu city) means "Is it trendy or not? Is it modern or not?", and the reply "好city啊" (hao city a, "so city!") can also mean "so exciting, so fun". It comes from 保保熊 (Bao Bao Xiong), an American creator living in Shanghai, who asked his sister "city不city啊?" in a catchy sing-song voice in videos of their travels in China. The clips went viral on Douyin in June 2024, and the phrase made the 《咬文嚼字》 (Yaowen Jiaozi) list of the top ten Chinese buzzwords of 2024.

body: City literally means a city, but in this meme it works as an adjective. Calling a place, an outfit or an experience "very city" means it is stylish, modern and a bit glamorous. The creator has said in interviews that anything that makes you feel lively, thrilled or excited can be "city", so even somewhere in the countryside can be "so city".
Part of the fun is the language mix: a foreigner drops an English word into the Chinese "X不X" (X or not X) question pattern, with an intonation that is hard to get out of your head.

head: Date
Event
rows: During his sister's visit to China, the two improvise "city不city啊?" / "好city啊!" while filming at the Great Wall
The "city不city" videos go viral on Douyin; he says one passed 10 million views about three hours after posting
By 11 July his Douyin account has over 760,000 followers and the phrase is everywhere online
《咬文嚼字》 names "city不city" No. 4 on its 2024 top ten buzzwords, the only entry with Latin letters

ul: About a place: "这条老街city不city？" "好city啊！" (Is this old street trendy? So trendy!)
Praising an outfit: "今天这身也太city了吧。" (This look is so city today.)
Self-mocking: "下班挤地铁，一点都不city。" (Squeezing onto the subway after work: not city at all.)
For something thrilling: "坐完过山车，好city啊！" (After the roller coaster: so city!)

body: Summer 2024 was its peak. Since then it has settled into everyday slang that every Chinese internet user understands, and it often shows up in travel, fashion and city-promotion headlines. Shouting "city不city" on its own is no longer fresh, but calling a place "very city" still sounds natural and friendly.

faq.a: 保保熊 (Bao Bao Xiong), an American creator living in Shanghai. His Q&A with his sister, "city不city啊?" / "好city啊!", in China travel videos went viral on Douyin in June 2024.
"So city": very stylish or modern, or very exciting and fun. The creator's own definition is that anything that makes you feel energized and excited is "city".

faq.q: Did it make any word-of-the-year lists?
faq.a: Yes. On 2 December 2024, the editors of the language magazine 《咬文嚼字》 put "city不city" at No. 4 on their top ten buzzwords of 2024.
